function: PPO jointly learns BS beamforming, STAR-RIS transmission/reflection phases and amplitudes, and video encoder bitrate to maximize total PSNR; MEC extension adds DROO offloading (pp. 5-6, 15).
system: Downlink MISO, BS with 8-12 antennas, 8-12 single-antenna users, 1-4 distributed STAR-RIS (N=4-16, energy splitting, amplitude-phase coupled), 50 kHz bandwidth, carrier frequency not stated (pp. 3, 8).
method: Reinforcement learning (PPO): Gaussian-policy actor-critic with GAE and clipped objective, MLP 1024-512-128-64 (downlink); MEC extension adds DROO network for offloading (pp. 6-8, 15-17).
data_channel: Synthetic CN(0,1) channels (Table 1, p. 8), estimation-error variance 1% or 5% of channel power (p. 9); video RD parameters fitted offline from H.264 encodes (pp. 4-5).
test_conditions: Agents trained and evaluated in one simulated topology per setting (Figs. 4-8, 12-14); CSI error 0%, 1%, 5%; no unseen-environment test (pp. 8-9, 17-18).
baselines: Learned only: STAR-RIS TD3 [9], RIS DDPG [13] (downlink); RIS-based PPO plus DROO [18] (MEC). No non-learned baseline (pp. 7, 9, 17).
metrics: Average PSNR (cross-layer video quality) vs time step; PSNR gain 3-4 dB single STAR-RIS, about 2 dB multi-STAR-RIS, 1-3 dB MEC; parameters, training/testing time, inference latency (pp. 8-9, 17).
complexity: Table 3 (p. 8): parameters 1,898,368 (PPO), 16,006,784 (TD3), 1,497,344 (DDPG); training 12757.6 s vs 4533.9 s (TD3); inference 8.52 ms vs 10.59 ms (TD3) per step (pp. 8-9).
q1_support: p. 7: "our simulation configurations reflect standardized benchmark topologies and traffic models" but no channel model is named; p. 8, Table 1: Channel Initialization CN(0,1). Synthetic complex Gaussian channels; no 3GPP, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured data.
q2_support: p. 18: "its generalizability to radically asymmetric spatial distributions without structural retraining are a known limitation of the current centralized DRL framework". Figs. 4-8 and 12-14 use separate settings of M, N, U, and p. 9 sweeps CSI error (1%, 5%); no unseen condition is tested.
q3_support: p. 7: "we compare it against two baseline methods: the STAR-RIS TD3 scheme [9] and the RIS DDPG scheme [13]"; p. 17: "comparing it against the baseline method [18]". All are learned; no random or fixed RIS, ZF/MMSE or optimization baseline is compared.
q4_support: p. 8: Table 3 lists total network parameters 1,898,368 (PPO), 16,006,784 (TD3), 1,497,344 (DDPG); p. 9: "achieving a lower average inference latency of 8.52 ms compared to 10.59 ms for TD3".
q5_support: No code or data link appears in the paper. p. 7: "To ensure the rigor and reproducibility of our evaluation, the simulation environment is established based on the physical parameters defined in Table 1" lists parameters only; channels are synthetic and no public dataset is named.
notes: Include, area 3: PPO learns BS beamforming and STAR-RIS coefficients jointly with video encoder bitrate, so the physical-layer decision passes the above_phy check; the MEC extension also learns STAR-RIS configuration with PPO and offloading with DROO (p. 15). Tables 1-6 and the figures were read from page images. q3 is 0 because every baseline is a learned DRL scheme (TD3, DDPG, PPO plus DROO); the robust MMSE-inspired error model (Eqs. 28-31, p. 7) is part of the proposed framework, not a compared baseline. The 1% and 5% CSI error cases are a sweep, not new conditions. Carrier frequency is not stated.
